extracted.intended_audience: JOSS editors, handling editors, reviewers, and Track Editors-in-Chief
extracted.subtask_short: JOSS editorial process for software papers
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and quality criteria for handling, reviewing, and publishing software papers submitted to the Journal of Open Source Software (JOSS), including pre-review screening gates, reviewer selection, review conduct, and post-review publication steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public development history ≥ 6 months
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the repository public for more than six months, with development activity distributed across that period?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A recent repo dump or commits concentrated into a short window fails this gate. Look at commit distribution over time, not just total commit count. This is a hard gate: submissions failing it should receive a desk rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstrated research impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Is there evidence the software is actually being used for research?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for paper/preprint references, DOIs, cited use by others, or documented integration into research workflows. Potential future use is not sufficient. This is a hard gate: lack of demonstrated impact should lead to desk rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open source practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the repository show the expected signals of an open project?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For multi-author projects: issues, PRs, public discussion. For single-author projects: at least several of — tagged releases/changelog, tests/CI, clear documentation, CONTRIBUTING file, stated support expectations. Multiple indicators must be present. Single-author projects should not be rejected solely for lacking a PR workflow if other signals are strong. This is a hard gate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Iterative development (commit history)
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the commit history show ongoing refinement rather than a one-time code dump?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inspect commit distribution over time (not just total commits) to assess iterative development. This is a hard gate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Borderline pre-review decision guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: How to handle submissions that don't clearly fail a single gate but fall short on several.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a submission doesn’t clearly fail any single gate but falls short on several, it can still be desk-rejected. Summarise the specific gaps in your rejection notice and encourage resubmission in six months once those gaps are addressed. See sample messages for rejection language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editor pre-review checklist (editor checks before finding reviewers)
rubrics_metrics.description: The editor looks at the software and checks to see if: there’s a general description of the software; the software is within scope as research software; it has an OSI-approved license.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It’s also worth re-checking the pre-review screening gates that the track EiC should have checked. If the paper is not in the default branch, add it to the issue using the bot command to set branch.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum number of reviewers and flexibility
rubrics_metrics.description: JOSS papers must have a minimum of two reviewers per submission (except for papers previously peer-reviewed via rOpenSci or pyOpenSci).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the editor feels unsure, recruit a third (or fourth) reviewer. Having at least three can help if one reviewer drops out so the review can continue with remaining reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer expertise coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Between the two or three reviewers, ensure all aspects of the submission are covered (language, scientific discipline, software practices, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is rare that all reviewers cover all aspects; deliberately choose reviewers so combined expertise covers the submission's needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adhere to JOSS conflict-of-interest (COI) policy in reviewer selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Selection and assignment of reviewers should adhere to the JOSS COI policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify suitability and conflicts before assigning reviewers; use the reviewer management mechanisms provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer recruitment methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommended ways to find and recruit reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the list of reviewers via editorialbot or the Reviewers Management System; search the reviewer application spreadsheet (watch reviewer load); ask authors to suggest reviewers (but instruct authors not to @-tag suggestions); use professional network, Google/GitHub search, social networks; check authors of referenced work or users of the software. Avoid asking JOSS editors to review if possible. When contacting potential reviewers, describe what JOSS is and what reviewing entails.

rubrics_metrics.name: Starting the review (editor actions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Commands and steps to start the formal review: assign reviewers, run @editorialbot start review to create the REVIEW issue with prepared checklists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you haven’t assigned an editor and reviewer, the bot will tell you. Move the conversation from pre-review to the REVIEW issue. If starting before all reviewers identified, editor may hand-edit the checklist to add space for later reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer checklist use and interaction norms
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers should generate their checklist and check off items one-by-one while engaging authors in conversation aimed at improving the paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers use @editorialbot generate my checklist. Editors should 'lurk' and intervene if needed (e.g., CoC issues). Keep comments in the REVIEW issue brief; post longer suggestions or requests as separate issues in the submission repository with a link-back to the review thread.

rubrics_metrics.name: Managing reviewer unresponsiveness and adding reviewers mid-review
rubrics_metrics.description: If a reviewer recants commitment or is unresponsive, editors can remove them or add new reviewers; newly added reviewers must generate checklists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use @editorialbot remove @username from reviewers to remove. To add: @editorialbot add @newreviewer as reviewer. New reviewers must run @editorialbot generate my checklist to get their checklist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-review archival and release requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: When ready to accept, ask authors to make a new tagged release of the software (if changed) and archive it on Zenodo, figshare, or other; authors post version number and archive DOI in the REVIEW issue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Update the review thread with the archive DOI using @editorialbot set <doi> as archive and set <version> as version. A new release is only necessary if the software changed during review; changes to the paper do not require a new release.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-publication proof and reference checks
rubrics_metrics.description: Before finalizing acceptance, generate a proof and check references have DOIs and that links work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors can run @editorialbot generate pdf and @editorialbot check references. Proof-read the paper and ask authors to fix typos, badly formed citations, awkward wording, etc. Use editorialbot create post-review checklist to get final steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Archive deposit metadata and author list consistency
rubrics_metrics.description: Check the archive deposit has correct metadata (title and author list) and that the author lists match between paper and archive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In most situations the two author lists should match. Other contributors can be present and should be marked. Check that all authors of the paper are in the archive metadata; if lists differ, ask for the reason and document it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommend-accept and EiC handoff
rubrics_metrics.description: If everything looks good, the handling editor uses @editorialbot recommend-accept to notify the EiC team and generate final proofs for publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After recommend-accept the EiC/AEiC will take over to make final checks and publish. Ask authors to check proofs to avoid post-publication author-list changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejecting a paper (scope flagging and communication)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a submission should be rejected (e.g., out of scope), flag it and communicate reasons to the author.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use @editorialbot query scope to add the query-scope label. Mention to the author your reasons and optionally give them an opportunity to defend their submission. The TEiC will make the final determination. During the scope review the editorial team may ask authors for additional information to assist the decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope review and resubmission handling
rubrics_metrics.description: How TEiC handles resubmissions and scope reviews for previously rejected papers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For resubmitted papers TEiC will use discretion to determine whether (1) a full scope review by the entire editorial team is necessary, (2) previous reasons remain valid, or (3) there have been enough updates to warrant sending the submission out for review.

rubrics_metrics.name: How papers are assigned to editors (TEiC assignment criteria)
rubrics_metrics.description: TEiC will attempt to assign an incoming paper to the most suitable handling editor but may assign to editors outside their domain in certain situations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Situations include: no obvious fit to any JOSS editors; the most suitable editor is already handling many papers; the chosen editor has a lighter editorial load. TEiC may ask one or more editors to edit; if an editor doesn’t respond within ~3 working days, TEiC may assign the paper regardless. Editors may also be invited via the bot.

rubrics_metrics.name: JOSS collaboration with AAS publishing — additional steps
rubrics_metrics.description: Additional editorial steps when the submission is a joint publication with an AAS journal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the AAS label to both pre-review and review issues. Before moving to review, inform reviewers that JOSS will receive a small donation from AAS publishing. After JOSS acceptance, ask the author for the AAS paper DOI and have them add it to paper.md YAML header (aas-doi, aas-journal fields). Optionally pause the review (apply paused label) to await AAS publication; once published, ask EiC on rotation to publish the JOSS paper.

rubrics_metrics.name: rOpenSci/pyOpenSci-streamlined review handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedure when a paper has already been reviewed and accepted by rOpenSci or pyOpenSci.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assign yourself as editor and reviewer, add a comment in pre-review pointing to the rOpenSci/pyOpenSci review, add the rOpenSci/pyOpenSci label, start the review issue, point to the prior review in the review issue, compile the paper and check it looks OK, grab the Zenodo DOI from the source repo, then accept and publish the paper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communication norms for reviewer invitations and author-suggested reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: How to solicit reviewers and handle author suggestions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mention potential reviewers in pre-review with their GitHub handle, ping them on social media, or email them. When asking the author to suggest reviewers, tell the author not to @-tag their suggestions. If asking candidate reviewers by email, include a longer explanation of JOSS and the review expectations; be mindful of reviewers' current load.
